p: Implement class `TextBuffer` with `insert(pos, text)`, `delete(pos, length)` (ValueError if out of range), `text()`, `undo()`, `redo()` (each returns True if something was undone/redone, else False), `begin_group()` / `end_group()` so that all edits between them undo as ONE step (groups may nest; only the outermost end closes the group), and `checkpoint()` returning an opaque token plus `revert(token)` restoring that exact state as a NEW undoable edit. A new edit after undo discards the redo stack. Each undo/redo must restore the text exactly; the test performs 50,000 random operations against a reference and cross-checks after every step, so store inverse operations rather than full copies (full copies of a 100 KB buffer per edit would exhaust the time limit).
t:
import random,time
b=TextBuffer(); b.insert(0,'hello'); b.insert(5,' world'); assert b.text()=='hello world'
assert b.undo() and b.text()=='hello' and b.redo() and b.text()=='hello world' and not b.redo()
b.delete(0,6); assert b.text()=='world'; b.undo(); assert b.text()=='hello world'
b.begin_group(); b.delete(0,5); b.insert(0,'HELLO'); b.begin_group(); b.insert(11,'!'); b.end_group(); b.end_group(); assert b.text()=='HELLO world!'
assert b.undo() and b.text()=='hello world' and b.redo() and b.text()=='HELLO world!'
tok=b.checkpoint(); b.insert(0,'>> '); b.delete(3,5); assert b.text()=='>>  world!'; b.revert(tok); assert b.text()=='HELLO world!'; b.undo(); assert b.text()=='>>  world!'
b.undo(); b.undo(); assert b.text()=='HELLO world!'; b.insert(0,'x'); assert not b.redo()
try: b.delete(100,1); assert False
except ValueError: pass
random.seed(43); b=TextBuffer(); hist=['']; ptr=0; cur=''; depth=0; grp_edits=False; t0=time.time()
for i in range(50000):
    op=random.random()
    if op<0.45:
        p=random.randint(0,len(cur)); s=''.join(random.choice('ab') for _ in range(random.randint(1,3))); b.insert(p,s); cur=cur[:p]+s+cur[p:]
        if depth==0: hist=hist[:ptr+1]+[cur]; ptr+=1
        else: grp_edits=True
    elif op<0.7 and cur:
        p=random.randint(0,len(cur)-1); L=random.randint(1,min(3,len(cur)-p)); b.delete(p,L); cur=cur[:p]+cur[p+L:]
        if depth==0: hist=hist[:ptr+1]+[cur]; ptr+=1
        else: grp_edits=True
    elif op<0.78:
        if depth==0: b.begin_group(); depth=1; grp_edits=False
        else:
            b.end_group(); depth=0
            if grp_edits: hist=hist[:ptr+1]+[cur]; ptr+=1
    elif op<0.9 and depth==0:
        r=b.undo()
        if ptr>0: assert r; ptr-=1; cur=hist[ptr]
        else: assert not r
    elif depth==0:
        r=b.redo()
        if ptr<len(hist)-1: assert r; ptr+=1; cur=hist[ptr]
        else: assert not r
    assert b.text()==cur,(i,)
assert time.time()-t0<40

p: Implement `parse_url(url)` per RFC 3986 returning a dict with keys scheme, userinfo, host, port (int or None), path, query (dict of lists, parsed with '&' and '=' and percent-decoding, '+' decoded to space), fragment. Rules: scheme is required and case-insensitive (return lowercase); host is lowercased; an IPv6 literal keeps its brackets; a port must be all digits (ValueError otherwise) and a port equal to the scheme default (http 80, https 443) is returned as None; percent-decoding of path and query components must decode %XX (uppercase or lowercase) and raise ValueError on a malformed % sequence; userinfo may contain a password ('user:pass'). Also `normalize(url)` returning the canonical string: lowercase scheme and host, default port removed, dot-segments in the path resolved ('/a/./b/../c' -> '/a/c'), empty path for a hierarchical URL becomes '/', percent-encoded unreserved characters decoded and hex digits uppercased in remaining escapes, and query pairs kept in original order.
t:
u=parse_url('HTTPS://User:Pa%40ss@Example.COM:443/a/b%20c?x=1&y=a+b&x=%41&z#frag')
assert u['scheme']=='https' and u['userinfo']=='User:Pa%40ss' and u['host']=='example.com' and u['port'] is None and u['path']=='/a/b c'
assert u['query']=={'x':['1','A'],'y':['a b'],'z':['']} and u['fragment']=='frag'
u=parse_url('http://[2001:db8::1]:8080/'); assert u['host']=='[2001:db8::1]' and u['port']==8080 and u['path']=='/' and u['query']=={} and u['fragment'] is None
u=parse_url('mailto:someone@example.com'); assert u['scheme']=='mailto' and u['host'] is None and u['path']=='someone@example.com'
for bad in ('http://host:abc/','http://h/%zz','nourl','http://h/a%2'):
    try: parse_url(bad); assert False,bad
    except ValueError: pass
assert normalize('HTTP://Example.com:80/a/./b/../c/%7ejoe/%3a?q=1&r=2')=='http://example.com/a/c/~joe/%3A?q=1&r=2'
assert normalize('https://x.org')=='https://x.org/' and normalize('http://x.org/../../a')=='http://x.org/a'
assert normalize('http://x.org/a/b/')=='http://x.org/a/b/' and normalize('http://x.org/a/b/.')=='http://x.org/a/b/'
assert normalize('http://x.org/p?b=2&a=1#f')=='http://x.org/p?b=2&a=1#f'

p: Implement byte-pair-encoding training and encoding over a corpus of words. `train_bpe(words, num_merges)` where words is a dict word -> count: start from the character sequence of each word plus a terminal '</w>' symbol; repeatedly count adjacent symbol pairs across all words (weighted by count), merge the most frequent pair (ties: lexicographically smallest pair tuple), stop early when no pair occurs at least twice; return the ordered list of merges as tuples. `encode(word, merges)` applies the merges in order to a new word (with '</w>') and returns the symbol list. `decode(symbols)` reverses it to the word. The merge list must be exactly reproducible.

Implement `dsatur(n, edges)` returning a proper vertex colouring of an undirected graph on nodes 0..n-1 as a list of colour indices (0-based, smallest possible first) using the DSATUR heuristic: repeatedly pick the uncoloured vertex with the highest saturation (number of distinct colours among its neighbours), breaking ties by highest degree, then lowest index; give it the smallest colour not used by its neighbours. Also `is_proper(n, edges, colours)` and `exact_chromatic(n, edges)` returning the exact chromatic number by backtracking with the DSATUR order (n <= 12 in the test). The test checks proper colourings and known chromatic numbers: bipartite 2, odd cycle 3, K5 5, Petersen 3, and the Mycielski graph of C5 (Grötzsch, 11 vertices) 4.
t:
import random
def K(n): return [(i,j) for i in range(n) for j in range(i+1,n)]
def cyc(n): return [(i,(i+1)%n) for i in range(n)]
petersen=[(i,(i+1)%5) for i in range(5)]+[(i,i+5) for i in range(5)]+[(5+i,5+(i+2)%5) for i in range(5)]
gr=[(i,(i+1)%5) for i in range(5)]+[(i,5+(i+1)%5) for i in range(5)]+[(i,5+(i-1)%5) for i in range(5)]+[(5+i,10) for i in range(5)]
for n,E,chi in ((6,[(0,3),(0,4),(1,3),(1,5),(2,4),(2,5)],2),(7,cyc(7),3),(5,K(5),5),(10,petersen,3),(11,gr,4),(1,[],1),(3,[],1)):
    c=dsatur(n,E); assert is_proper(n,E,c) and len(c)==n and min(c)==0 and max(c)+1>=chi and exact_chromatic(n,E)==chi,(n,chi,c)
assert dsatur(4,cyc(4))==[0,1,0,1] and dsatur(5,K(5))==[0,1,2,3,4]
assert not is_proper(3,cyc(3),[0,0,1])
random.seed(45)
for _ in range(40):
    n=random.randint(2,10); E=[(i,j) for i in range(n) for j in range(i+1,n) if random.random()<0.4]
    c=dsatur(n,E); assert is_proper(n,E,c) and exact_chromatic(n,E)<=max(c)+1 and max(c)+1<=exact_chromatic(n,E)+2

p: Implement the Burrows-Wheeler transform with an end-of-string sentinel: `bwt(s)` returns the last column of the sorted rotations of s + '\x00' (the sentinel sorts before every other character; s must not contain '\x00', else ValueError); `ibwt(t)` inverts it. Then `mtf_encode(t)` / `mtf_decode(codes)` move-to-front over the byte alphabet 0..255 (initial list in ascending order; input is a str whose chars are all < 256), and `rle_encode(codes)` / `rle_encode` inverse `rle_decode` using the scheme: a run of the same value v of length L (1..255) becomes [v, L]. `compress(s)` chains bwt -> mtf -> rle and `decompress` reverses it. Must handle a 200,000-character input within a few seconds, so build the BWT with sorted suffix ranks (doubling) or a suffix array rather than materialising all rotations as strings.
t:
import random,time
assert bwt('banana')=='annb\x00aa' and ibwt('annb\x00aa')=='banana' and bwt('')=='\x00' and ibwt('\x00')==''
try: bwt('a\x00b'); assert False
except ValueError: pass
assert mtf_encode('aab')==[97,0,98] and mtf_decode([97,0,98])=='aab' and mtf_encode('')==[]
assert rle_encode([5,5,5,2])==[5,3,2,1] and rle_decode([5,3,2,1])==[5,5,5,2] and rle_encode([7]*300)==[7,255,7,45]
random.seed(46)
for _ in range(200):
    s=''.join(random.choice('ab') for _ in range(random.randint(0,40)))
    assert ibwt(bwt(s))==s and decompress(compress(s))==s and mtf_decode(mtf_encode(s))==s
for s in ('mississippi','abracadabra'*3,'zzzz'):
    assert ibwt(bwt(s))==s and decompress(compress(s))==s
random.seed(47); big=''.join(random.choice('acgt') for _ in range(200000)); t0=time.time(); assert ibwt(bwt(big))==big and time.time()-t0<30
rep='abcabc'*30000; assert len(compress(rep))<len(rep)//10 and decompress(compress(rep))==rep

p: Implement `matrix_chain(dims)` where dims is a list of n+1 integers describing n matrices (matrix i has shape dims[i] x dims[i+1]). Return (min_scalar_multiplications, parenthesization) where the parenthesization is a string using A1..An and full explicit parentheses around every product, e.g. '((A1A2)A3)'; when several splits tie, choose the SMALLEST split index k. Also `evaluate_chain(matrices, parenthesization)` that multiplies the given list of integer matrices (lists of lists) in the order given by the parenthesization string and returns the product, and `count_multiplications(dims, parenthesization)` returning the scalar multiplications that order costs. n up to 300 must finish in a few seconds (O(n^3) DP).
t:
assert matrix_chain([10,20,30])==(6000,'(A1A2)') and matrix_chain([10,20,30,40,30])==(30000,'((A1(A2A3))A4)') and matrix_chain([5])==(0,'A1') if False else True
assert matrix_chain([10,20,30])==(6000,'(A1A2)')
assert matrix_chain([10,20,30,40,30])==(30000,'(((A1A2)A3)A4)')
assert matrix_chain([40,20,30,10,30])==(26000,'((A1(A2A3))A4)')
assert matrix_chain([5,10])==(0,'A1')
r=matrix_chain([2,2,2,2]); assert r[0]==16 and r[1]=='(A1(A2A3))', r
A=[[1,2],[3,4]]; B=[[5,6],[7,8]]; C=[[1,0],[0,1]]
assert evaluate_chain([A,B,C],'((A1A2)A3)')==[[19,22],[43,50]] and evaluate_chain([A,B,C],'(A1(A2A3))')==[[19,22],[43,50]]
assert count_multiplications([10,20,30,40,30],'((A1(A2A3))A4)')==44000 and count_multiplications([10,20,30,40,30],'(((A1A2)A3)A4)')==30000
import random,time; random.seed(48)
for _ in range(30):
    n=random.randint(1,7); dims=[random.randint(1,9) for _ in range(n+1)]
    cost,par=matrix_chain(dims); assert count_multiplications(dims,par)==cost
    import itertools
    def allp(i,j):
        if i==j: return [f'A{i+1}']
        return ['('+l+r+')' for k in range(i,j) for l in allp(i,k) for r in allp(k+1,j)]
    assert cost==min(count_multiplications(dims,p) for p in allp(0,n-1))
dims=[random.randint(1,50) for _ in range(301)]; t0=time.time(); matrix_chain(dims); assert time.time()-t0<25

p: Implement an event-sourced bank ledger. Class `Ledger` with `apply(event)` where event is a dict with keys id (unique string; a duplicate id is IGNORED and returns False — idempotency), type in {'open','deposit','withdraw','transfer','close'}, and fields account / amount / from / to as appropriate; amounts are positive ints. Rules: operations on unknown or closed accounts raise ValueError; withdraw/transfer must not overdraw; 'close' only when balance is 0. `apply` returns True when the event changed state. `balance(account)`, `history(account)` (list of applied event ids affecting it, in order), `snapshot()` returning {account: balance}, `replay(events)` rebuilding from scratch (must be idempotent: replaying the same list twice gives the same state), and `rollback(event_id)` undoing that event AND every later applied event, returning the list of undone ids (raise KeyError if unknown). A rejected event (ValueError) must leave state unchanged and not count as applied.
t:
L=Ledger()
assert L.apply({'id':'e1','type':'open','account':'A'}) and L.apply({'id':'e2','type':'deposit','account':'A','amount':100})
assert not L.apply({'id':'e2','type':'deposit','account':'A','amount':100}) and L.balance('A')==100
assert L.apply({'id':'e3','type':'open','account':'B'}) and L.apply({'id':'e4','type':'transfer','from':'A','to':'B','amount':30}) and L.snapshot()=={'A':70,'B':30}
for bad in ({'id':'x1','type':'withdraw','account':'A','amount':500},{'id':'x2','type':'deposit','account':'Z','amount':1},{'id':'x3','type':'close','account':'A'},{'id':'x4','type':'transfer','from':'B','to':'A','amount':31}):
    try: L.apply(bad); assert False,bad
    except ValueError: pass
assert L.snapshot()=={'A':70,'B':30} and L.history('A')==['e1','e2','e4'] and L.history('B')==['e3','e4']
assert L.apply({'id':'e5','type':'withdraw','account':'B','amount':30}) and L.apply({'id':'e6','type':'close','account':'B'})
try: L.apply({'id':'x5','type':'deposit','account':'B','amount':1}); assert False
except ValueError: pass
assert L.rollback('e4')==['e4','e5','e6'] and L.snapshot()=={'A':100,'B':0} and L.history('A')==['e1','e2']
try: L.rollback('nope'); assert False
except KeyError: pass
assert L.apply({'id':'e4','type':'transfer','from':'A','to':'B','amount':30}) and L.snapshot()=={'A':70,'B':30}
evs=[{'id':'a','type':'open','account':'X'},{'id':'b','type':'deposit','account':'X','amount':5},{'id':'b','type':'deposit','account':'X','amount':5}]
M=Ledger(); M.replay(evs); M.replay(evs); assert M.snapshot()=={'X':5} and M.history('X')==['a','b']

p: Implement univariate polynomial arithmetic over the rationals using fractions.Fraction, representing a polynomial as a list of coefficients from the constant term upward with NO trailing zeros (the zero polynomial is []). Functions: `p_add`, `p_sub`, `p_mul`, `p_divmod(a, b)` (ValueError on division by zero polynomial), `p_gcd(a, b)` returning the MONIC greatest common divisor, `p_eval(p, x)`, `p_deriv(p)`, `p_pow(p, n)`, `p_str(p)` rendering like '3/2x^2 - x + 1' (see tests for exact format), and `p_roots_rational(p)` returning the sorted list of rational roots (rational root theorem on integer-scaled coefficients, each root once). The test checks (x^2-1)/(x-1), gcd((x^2-1),(x^2-2x+1)) = x - 1, and a degree-200 multiply/divide round trip.
t:
from fractions import Fraction as F
x2m1=[F(-1),F(0),F(1)]; xm1=[F(-1),F(1)]
assert p_add([1,2],[3])==[F(4),F(2)] and p_sub([1,2],[1,2])==[] and p_mul(xm1,[1,1])==x2m1 and p_mul([],[1,2])==[]
assert p_divmod(x2m1,xm1)==([F(1),F(1)],[]) and p_divmod([1],[1,1])==([],[F(1)]) and p_divmod([1,3,2],[2])==([F(1,2),F(3,2),F(1)],[])
try: p_divmod([1],[]); assert False
except ValueError: pass
assert p_gcd(x2m1,[1,-2,1])==[F(-1),F(1)] and p_gcd([2,4],[3,6])==[F(1,2),F(1)] and p_gcd([],[2,4])==[F(1,2),F(1)] and p_gcd([5],[7])==[F(1)]
assert p_eval([1,2,3],2)==F(17) and p_eval([],5)==0 and p_deriv([1,2,3])==[F(2),F(6)] and p_deriv([7])==[] and p_pow([1,1],3)==[F(1),F(3),F(3),F(1)] and p_pow([2,1],0)==[F(1)]
assert p_str([1,-1,F(3,2)])=='3/2x^2 - x + 1' and p_str([])=='0' and p_str([0,1])=='x' and p_str([-2,0,-1])=='-x^2 - 2' and p_str([F(1,3)])=='1/3' and p_str([0,-1])=='-x' and p_str([1,2])=='2x + 1'
assert p_roots_rational([-6,11,-6,1])==[F(1),F(2),F(3)] and p_roots_rational([-1,0,2])==[] and p_roots_rational([1,-2,1])==[F(1)] and p_roots_rational([0,0,1])==[F(0)] and p_roots_rational([2,-7,3])==[F(1,3),F(2)] and p_roots_rational([F(-1,2),F(1)])==[F(1,2)]
import random; random.seed(49)
a=[F(random.randint(-9,9)) for _ in range(201)]; b=[F(random.randint(-9,9)) for _ in range(101)]
while not b[-1]: b[-1]=F(1)
while not a[-1]: a[-1]=F(1)
q,r=p_divmod(p_mul(a,b),b); assert q==a and r==[]
